description:
The Pichda Varg Post Matric Chhatravritti is a significant welfare scheme initiated by the Government of India aimed at providing financial assistance to students from backward classes pursuing higher education. 

This scheme was launched in the year 2006. 

It is specifically designed to support students who belong to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes. 

The primary objective of the Pichda Varg Post Matric Chhatravritti is to ensure that students from these communities have access to higher education without financial constraints. 

The scheme aims to reduce dropout rates among students from backward classes by providing them with the necessary financial support. 

The target is to increase the enrollment of students from these communities in post-matriculation courses. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme covers various expenses including tuition fees, maintenance allowances, and other educational costs. 

Eligible students can receive a scholarship amount ranging from INR 1,200 to INR 3,000 per month depending on the course and institution. 

The maintenance allowance is provided for a maximum of 10 months in an academic year. 

For students pursuing professional courses, the scholarship amount can be as high as INR 2,000 per month. 

In addition to the maintenance allowance, students are also eligible for reimbursement of tuition fees. 

The maximum tuition fee reimbursement can go up to INR 10,000 per annum. 

The eligibility criteria for the Pichda Varg Post Matric Chhatravritti scheme include students who belong to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, or Other Backward Classes. 

Students must be enrolled in a recognized post-matriculation course. 

The annual income of the student's family should not exceed INR 2.5 lakhs. 

Students must have secured at least 50% marks in their previous examinations to qualify for the scholarship. 

The application process for the Pichda Varg Post Matric Chhatravritti involves several steps. 

First, eligible students must visit the official website of the respective state government or the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

They need to fill out the online application form available on the portal. 

Students must provide necessary documents including caste certificates, income certificates, and academic records. 

The application must be submitted before the deadline set by the respective state government. 

After submission, the application will be verified by the concerned authorities. 

Once verified, the scholarship amount will be disbursed directly to the student’s bank account. 

The timeline for the application process varies from state to state. 

Typically, the application window opens in June and closes by August each year. 

Disbursement of funds usually occurs within two months after the application deadline. 

The implementing authority for the Pichda Varg Post Matric Chhatravritti scheme is the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

Each state has its own respective department that oversees the implementation of the scheme. 

For instance, in Maharashtra, the scheme is managed by the Social Justice and Special Assistance Department. 

Students can contact the state helpline numbers for assistance regarding the application process. 

In Maharashtra, the helpline number is 1800 120 8040. 

In Uttar Pradesh, the scheme is administered by the Backward Classes Welfare Department. 

The contact number for assistance in Uttar Pradesh is 0522 223 1166. 

The Pichda Varg Post Matric Chhatravritti scheme has seen significant uptake since its inception. 

According to the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, over 1.5 million students have benefited from the scheme in the last academic year. 

The government allocates a substantial budget for this scheme every year. 

In the financial year 2022-2023, the allocation was approximately INR 1,200 crores. 

This funding is aimed at covering the costs of scholarships for students from backward classes. 

The scheme has been instrumental in promoting educational equity and social justice. 

It has contributed to increasing the literacy rates among Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. 

The government regularly reviews and updates the scheme to ensure its effectiveness. 

In recent years, there has been a push to digitize the application process to make it more accessible. 

Students can now track their application status online through the official portal. 

The scheme also encourages students to pursue higher education in fields that are traditionally underrepresented among backward classes. 

This includes engineering, medicine, and other professional courses. 

The Pichda Varg Post Matric Chhatravritti is part of a larger framework of welfare schemes aimed at uplifting marginalized communities in India. 

It complements other initiatives such as the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme and the National Fellowship for Scheduled Castes. 

The government continuously seeks feedback from beneficiaries to improve the scheme. 

Awareness campaigns are also conducted to inform eligible students about the benefits of the scheme. 

The Pichda Varg Post Matric Chhatravritti has played a crucial role in empowering students from backward classes. 

By alleviating financial burdens, it has enabled many to pursue their academic and career aspirations. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to inclusive education. 

It reflects the broader goal of achieving social equity in India. 

Overall, the Pichda Varg Post Matric Chhatravritti scheme stands as a vital support system for students from marginalized backgrounds. 

It continues to evolve and adapt to the changing educational landscape of the country. 

The impact of this scheme is evident in the increasing number of students from backward classes enrolling in higher education institutions. 

This initiative not only fosters individual growth but also contributes to the socio-economic development of the nation. 

The Pichda Varg Post Matric Chhatravritti is an essential component of India's educational welfare policies. 

It serves as a model for similar initiatives aimed at promoting access to education for all.
